quotes.text: People ask, ‘Jeff, what’s struck you the most about your first year in Congress?’ There’s a lot of things that have surprised me, but AI and data centers and what they mean for our economy is probably the biggest surprise.

I’m concerned that if we have various states implementing AI rules on a piecemeal basis, we are going to impair the economy. [...] Please push us. Hold us accountable to get something done at the federal level.

America should lead the world in artificial intelligence, and that leadership starts with secure and reliable systems. This bipartisan bill creates a practical framework to identify and address vulnerabilities before they can be exploited, helping strengthen trust in AI while supporting continued innovation. I’m proud to work across the aisle to ensure the United States remains the global leader in developing and deploying these technologies.

As Chairman of the House Subcommittee on Indian and Insular Affairs, I recently chaired a hearing on the Missing and Murdered Indigenous People crisis.

One point came through clearly: in many cases, the technology to solve these cases already exists. The challenge is making sure it’s actually used.

Witnesses described how advanced DNA analysis and AI are helping solve cold cases and identify remains that once had no leads.

Families who have waited years for answers deserve every available tool in the pursuit of justice. I’ll keep working to remove the barriers that stand in the way. #CO03

When a wildfire starts, every minute matters.

At a hearing on disaster prevention, I asked John Gale of Pano AI how faster detection can help firefighters respond sooner.

In Douglas County, Pano’s system alerted response agencies within minutes of detecting the Bear Creek Fire. A local helitack crew responded, and the fire was contained to less than three acres.

Technology like this can give firefighters something they rarely have enough of: time. #CO03
